name: Al-Ghazali leaves teaching for Sufism
summary: Abu Hamid al-Ghazali, then the leading scholar of the Nizamiyya in Baghdad, abandons his teaching position for a decade of Sufi wandering. He returns to write Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din ('The Revival of the Religious Sciences'), reconciling Sunni orthodoxy with Sufi mysticism.

_quarry.structural_significance: Decisive integration of Sufism into Sunni orthodoxy; al-Ghazali's synthesis becomes the standard mediation between juristic and mystical Islam for the following centuries.
